title: Joe Venuti and Eddie Lang as colleagues
summary: Challis never found Venuti difficult, used him and Lang on Goldkette sessions, and worked with Lang later.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Let's go back and talk about some of the personalities that you were associated with, some of your impressions and reminiscences. For instance, we talked about Venuti and he had this reputation for being this wild prankster and even with a mean streak in him and ready to fight at the drop of a hat --

I didn't hear that until late. I never got that. I always got very nice treatment from Joe but actually I put him into some good spots. I mean Goldkette thing, everything we did, I had Joe and Eddie in there.
I was responsible for putting them in, the way I did put them in and it went smoothly, easily and we had no problem.

Now, I worked with Eddie after on several shows around the studios. I worked with Joe on one or two of them. But Joe, I never had that problem. It's always been laughs. Now I hear later he got to be a tough guy to get along with. But as I say I didn't find that.

Fine. Very good musicians. I would like to have used Joe in something that I had done rather -- I had an opportunity to do some things for him because O'Keefe was his manager for awhile, and booked him when he had a band. I went around with O'Keefe to listen to him.
He had a big band for awhile.
